steps.tx: A **prolactinoma** represents the most common functioning pituitary adenoma encountered in clinical endocrinology. True prolactin-secreting lactotroph adenomas must be distinguished from nonfunctioning sellar macroadenomas causing hyperprolactinaemia through pituitary stalk compression, commonly designated the **stalk effect**. Stalk compression disrupts physiological hypothalamic dopamine transport to normal lactotrophs, typically resulting in modest hyperprolactinaemia with serum prolactin concentrations remaining below 100 to 200 mcg/L.
steps.say: A prolactinoma is the most common functioning pituitary adenoma. It must be differentiated from nonfunctioning sellar tumours that cause hyperprolactinaemia via the stalk effect. Stalk compression interrupts dopamine delivery and produces modest prolactin elevations below 100 to 200 mcg/L, whereas true macroprolactinomas cause much higher elevations.

vis.caption: Sellar MRI demonstrating pituitary prolactinoma and stalk relationship. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The selective D2 receptor agonist **cabergoline** represents first-line medical therapy for prolactinoma, demonstrating superior efficacy and tolerability over short-acting **bromocriptine**. As an ergot-derived **dopamine agonist**, cabergoline normalizes circulating prolactin concentrations and achieves substantial tumour shrinkage in over 80% to 90% of microadenomas and macroadenomas. Transsphenoidal surgery is reserved for patients refractory to medical management or those experiencing progressive visual compromise from apoplexy.
steps.say: Cabergoline is first-line drug therapy for prolactinoma because it normalizes prolactin and shrinks tumours more effectively than bromocriptine. As a potent dopamine agonist, it produces significant tumour reduction in most patients. Neurosurgical resection is reserved for medication intolerance, treatment resistance, or acute visual decline.

vis.caption: Hypothalamic-pituitary lactotroph cell showing dopamine agonist cabergoline suppressing prolactin exocytosis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Clinicians must obtain a surveillance baseline and periodic transthoracic echocardiogram to monitor for cardiac **valvular regurgitation** when **cabergoline** is administered at cumulative high doses. While standard prolactinoma doses of 0.5 to 1.0 mg weekly carry negligible cardiac risk, cumulative weekly doses exceeding 2 mg per week for prolonged periods can stimulate serotonin 5-HT2B receptors on cardiac valvular interstitial cells, producing fibrotic valvular thickening and regurgitation.
steps.say: Echocardiographic surveillance is recommended when cabergoline is administered at doses above 2 mg per week for prolonged durations. High cumulative agonist exposure stimulates cardiac serotonin 5-HT2B receptors, which can lead to fibrotic valvular thickening and clinically significant valvular regurgitation.

steps.tx: Before committing an asymptomatic patient to therapy for moderately raised prolactin, clinicians must exclude **macroprolactin** by precipitating serum with polyethylene glycol. Macroprolactin consists of high-molecular-weight prolactin-IgG autoantibody complexes with minimal in vivo bioactivity. Furthermore, in patients with giant pituitary macroadenomas and unexpectedly mild prolactin elevations, serial serum dilution is mandatory to overcome assay saturation from the high-dose **hook effect**.
steps.say: Before treating mildly elevated prolactin, clinicians should precipitate serum with polyethylene glycol to rule out macroprolactin. In giant pituitary macroadenomas presenting with falsely modest prolactin levels, serial sample dilution is essential to eliminate the high-dose hook effect.

right.title: Hook Effect Artefact
points: Assay antibodies saturated by excess antigen
Falsely low or normal reported result

steps.tx: In women with a **microprolactinoma**, guidelines advise discontinuing dopamine agonist therapy as soon as **pregnancy** is confirmed, because the risk of clinically significant tumour enlargement during gestation remains below 2% to 3%. Conversely, in macroprolactinoma with optochiasmatic proximity, treatment with **bromocriptine** may be continued throughout gestation due to its extensive established safety profile in pregnancy, monitoring visual fields closely.
steps.say: In women with a microprolactinoma, discontinue dopamine agonist therapy once pregnancy is confirmed because gestation-associated tumour expansion is rare. For macroadenomas with chiasmal abutment, bromocriptine can be maintained throughout gestation given its documented fetal safety profile and close visual field monitoring.

rows: Assess only if headaches or visual symptoms occur

steps.tx: Second-generation antipsychotics, most notably **risperidone**, and dopamine-blocking antiemetics such as **metoclopramide** frequently induce symptomatic **drug-induced hyperprolactinemia**. By exerting potent D2 receptor antagonism at the median eminence outside the blood-brain barrier, these agents eliminate tonic dopaminergic inhibition. Serum prolactin frequently rises to 100 to 200 mcg/L, causing secondary hypogonadism, amenorrhoea, erectile dysfunction, and galactorrhoea in the absence of a sellar mass.
steps.say: Second-generation antipsychotics like risperidone and antiemetics like metoclopramide commonly induce drug-induced hyperprolactinemia through pituitary D2 receptor blockade. Circulating prolactin often reaches 100 to 200 mcg/L, producing symptomatic hypogonadism, amenorrhoea, and galactorrhoea.

left.title: Drug-Induced Hyperprolactinemia
points: D2 receptor antagonism at median eminence
Normal pituitary anatomy on contrast MRI
Normalizes within 48 to 72 hours of drug cessation

right.title: Prolactinoma Secretion
points: Prolactin level correlates directly with tumor size

steps.tx: True **dopamine agonist resistance** is defined as the inability to achieve biochemical prolactin normalization or at least 50% tumour volume reduction despite escalating doses of **cabergoline** up to 2 mg or more per week. Resistant prolactinomas more frequently occur in men, exhibit invasive suprasellar or cavernous sinus expansion, and harbor aggressive histologic features with elevated Ki-67 labeling index, often requiring transsphenoidal debulking, radiation, or temozolomide.
steps.say: Dopamine agonist resistance occurs when maximum tolerated doses of cabergoline fail to normalize prolactin or reduce tumour volume by half. Resistant tumours are more common in men and frequently exhibit aggressive cavernous sinus invasion requiring multimodal surgical, radiation, or alkylating chemotherapy.

right.title: Dopamine Agonist Resistant
points: D2 receptor down-regulation or low expression
Requires surgery, stereotactic radiotherapy, or temozolomide

steps.tx: Hyperprolactinaemia typically presents in premenopausal women with spontaneous or expressive **galactorrhea**, oligomenorrhoea, or secondary amenorrhoea. In men, clinical presentation is characteristically insidious, manifesting primarily with hypogonadotrophic **hypogonadism**, decreased libido, erectile dysfunction, oligospermia, and visual field deficits from macroadenoma compression. Prolactin suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility, leading directly to subnormal luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone secretion.
steps.say: Hyperprolactinaemia presents in premenopausal women with galactorrhea, oligomenorrhoea, and anovulatory infertility. In men, presentation is characteristically delayed, manifesting as hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, erectile dysfunction, and compressive visual defects from neglected macroadenomas.

rows: Suppression of hypothalamic GnRH pulse generator
